root_cause.text: The Rust Binder shrinker callback `rust_shrink_free_page()` incorrectly re-acquired the `list_lru` lock before returning, even though after the `mm/list_lru` per-cgroup locking change the shrinker path already held that same `lru->lock`, causing recursive locking and deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the forward-port "neglected to take commit fb56fdf8b9a2 ('mm/list_lru: split the lock to per-cgroup scope') into account" and reports `kswapd0` "already holding lock ... at: rust_helper_spin_lock" while trying to acquire `&l->lock` again in `lock_list_lru_of_memcg`; the patch fixes this by deleting `unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };` from `rust_shrink_free_page()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unintended re-acquisition of the LRU spinlock in the drop path so the cleanup returns without leaving the lock incorrectly locked.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a three-line block at the end of `drop(self: Pin<&mut Self>)` that re-acquired `(*lru).lock` via `unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };` after dropping `mm` and `page`, along with its accompanying safety comment.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer re-locks the LRU spinlock before returning, so the drop path leaves the lock unlocked instead of restoring it to a locked state. This changes lock state management and avoids taking an extra spin lock in this cleanup path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body of `rust_shrink_free_page()` clearly shows the vulnerable locking pattern, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause is re-acquiring the `list_lru` lock before returning from the shrinker callback. That exact construct is present here: after isolating the item and dropping references, the callback explicitly unlocks and then re-locks `lru->lock` using `bindings::spin_unlock(&raw mut (*lru).lock)` and later `bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock)`. Specifically, the code says `// SAFETY: The lru lock is locked when this method is called.` followed by `spin_unlock`, and at the end says `// SAFETY: We just unlocked the lru lock, but it should be locked when we return.` followed by `spin_lock`. Per the vulnerability description, after the `mm/list_lru` per-cgroup locking change, the shrinker path already holds this same `lru->lock`, so re-acquiring it in the callback creates recursive locking/deadlock. There is no alternative handling or conditional logic here to avoid re-locking under the new semantics, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet applied.
